context: Hiroshi-elder reads the morning newspaper aloud to Sho-young, explaining.
purpose: Elder patiently translating news for child.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 今朝の新聞、ようけ記事あるな。
lines.en: There's quite a lot in this morning's paper, isn't there.
lines.style: Slow, measured opening. Warm observation without urgency. Eyes on the page. Kansai cadence, patient and unhurried. Inviting the boy to look too.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: おじいちゃん、政治の話?
lines.style: Soft curiosity, genuinely wondering. No performance. Leans slightly forward with interest. Small voice but steady attention. Testing whether he'll explain.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: おう、報道、毎日、いろんな事件や。
lines.en: Yeah — the news, every day, all kinds of things happening.
lines.style: Gentle affirmation. Matter-of-fact but not dismissive. Slight settling back into the chair. Kansai warmth underneath. Opens the paper a little wider, inviting him closer.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 当時、おじいちゃんの時代、どうやった?
lines.en: Back when you were young, how was it different?
lines.style: Thoughtful pause before the question. Not asking for a lecture — genuinely wondering. Small voice but the question carries real weight. Waiting patiently for the answer.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: まったく違うで、新聞、ようけ家に届いた。
lines.en: Completely different. Papers got delivered to so many homes back then.
lines.style: Slight smile in the voice. Kansai lilt on the reminiscence. Slow, settling into memory. Hand touches the paper fondly. Not wistful, just — recalling what was.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 今、紙、残ってる家、少ない?
lines.en: Not many homes have newspapers anymore, do they?
lines.style: Quiet realization dawning. Not sad — observing. Small, thoughtful tone. A six-year-old noticing the gap between then and now. Waiting to see if grandpa agrees.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: うん、時代、変わったな、ほんま。
lines.en: Yeah. Times really have changed, haven't they.
lines.style: Soft agreement. Not resignation — just acceptance. Kansai warmth. Gentle exhale at the end. Holds the paper steady. The kind of quiet that invites sitting together without talking.
